definition: Evan! Renata and Lenin have a knack for having the most adorable babies ever (see Acatoddler). Evan has been a Wiessman since the day he was born and would love to meet you!
The Wiess courtyard/quad. The social epicenter of Wiess, where people commonly hang out, play frisbee or football, and study.
Giant covered swinging picnic table of glory, located in the Acabowl.
The grill located in the Acabowl.
The terrace behind the Upper Commons that we share with Hanszen.
Gavin! Almost six years old, Renata and Lenin’s adorable son is often found playing in the Acabowl. Feel free to join him and enjoy a study break.
The trampoline located in the Acabowl.

Fellows who also serve a specialized role during O-Week and afterwards. They include your Peer Academic Advisors, Diversity Facilitators, Rice Health Advisors, Gophers, Photographer, and Videographer.
Formal dinner held in the Commons once a semester to honor our Associates.
Fourth floor balcony. Great spot to hang out or watch the sunset.
The area under the Commons used for storage and shirt screening.
Affectionate name for the Wiess powderpuff football team.
Governing body of Wiess, made up entirely of Wiessmen. Meets every other Wednesday at 10pm in the Upper Commons. There’s always free food.
The place to be. You will eat here, study here, act here, play here, party here, hang out here, and well, live here.
A day filled with college bonding, hanging out, a nice dinner, and an evening of entertainment. Each college has their own each semester, usually with a different theme.
To pull up an extra chair at the corner of a table. Frequently occurs during meals but not at formal occasions.

Advisors for new Wiessmen. They are some of the greatest people you will ever meet and care about you so much. Co-Fellows are Fellows from other colleges. These other colleges may confuse you by calling them “advisors”—it’s the same position, we just call them something different.
24-hour film marathon held once a semester.
First Tabletop production of the year, which includes—you guessed it—one-acts featuring new students.
Four hours of required service hours. Necessary to enter the housing jack at the end of your first year. There are plenty of opportunities throughout the year to get them!
The official Wiess color. It will soon dominate your wardrobe. Remember, it’s not yellow!
The people who have been planning your O-Week since January. AKA Abbey, Eugene, and Richard. Be sure to come and say hi!
Called Academic Fellows at other colleges, Wiess Mentors are here to help you in your classes through review sessions or individual tutoring sessions.
Night of Decadence, Rice’s biggest party. Held at Wiess in October, featuring interesting decorations and creative costumes.
Off-campus Lounge. Room on first floor where people who live off-campus hang out.
Private dining room, a smaller room attached to the Commons.
The spreading of Halloween cheer, led by the elected College Idiots. Features Halloween songs and visits to the other colleges.
Process used to assign rooms for the next year.
Where you get your food before you go sit down in the Commons. We share South Servery with Hanszen.
The hidden room on the fourth floor, adorned with goldenrod paint, an air hockey table, and a mini basketball game system.
The loud speakers that can be heard throughout the Acabowl on Friday afternoons or special occasions.
Weekend retreat during the fall semester to discuss Wiess issues and bond with other Wiessmen.
Wiess theatre productions, held in the Commons.
Held during the spring semester, when Wiess hangs out in the Acabowl all day to eat good food and participate in various fun activities.
Our cheer—the embodiment of everything that makes Wiess cool.
An abbreviation of Team Family (or anything else that starts with F) Wiess.
Party to celebrate the new Cabinet held at Willy’s Pub each year.
A unique Wiess celebration of life.
Second floor of the Commons, featuring a pool table, ping pong table, foosball table, TV, and lots of couches.
Wiess mascot, embodied by the giant wooden pig built by the Class of 2012 for Beer Bike.
The Schaefer’s home. Where everybody knows your name, and the door is always open.
The inclusive, gender-neutral term for all of the members of Wiess—including you.
The three slabs of granite located in the Engineering Quad, worth three million dollars and modeled after their namesake angles.
Humanities or Social Sciences major. Very archaic term.
The central academic quadrangle around Willy’s Statue.
Architecture student.
Alternative Spring Break; service trip over spring break based on a social issue.
Faculty, staff, or community member associated with a college. Good people to get to know.
Gym in Tudor Fieldhouse where the Rice basketball team plays.

An event where participants undress, smear shaving cream on their bodies, and run around campus, leaving a trail of body prints. A proud Baker institution for over thirty years; all undergrads are invited to participate.
The James A. Baker III Institute for Public Policy. Holds a lot of interesting talks and events that are typically open to undergraduates. Not to be confused with Baker College.

A competitive intercollege race held in the spring, where ten bikers and ten chuggers from each college compete for both personal and college pride. Often compared to Christmas, and also includes a water balloon fight and much rejoicing.
The “real world” outside of Rice.
Classes frequently taken by Science and Engineering majors: Physics, Chemistry, and Calculus.
Bioscience Research Collaborative, where Rice meets the Texas Medical Center for research. Also where Bioengineers spend most of their time for class starting junior year.
A modernistic glass building located behind Fondren. Home to Salento (a non-student operated coffeeshop) and a great place to relax and sit outside.
1. The bell tower in the Engineering Quad, 2. Rice’s yearbook, 3. the undergraduate orchestra for non-music majors
An affectionate name for Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering majors.
Student-run coffeeshop providing the best legal way to artificially increase your study skills on short notice. Located in the RMC.
The faculty dining club near Sewall Hall with really good food.

Refers to distribution credits, Rice’s way of making sure you get a balanced education. You need 12 credit hours in each category to graduate. D1 = Humanities, D2 = Social Sciences, D3 = Science and Engineering.
The Digital Media Center. Lots of computers to use and cool equipment to check out. Located in the basement of Fondren Library.
Fall formal hosted by Rice Program Council. A major part of homecoming weekend and lots of fun!

Also known as Fondy or Club Fondy. Rice’s library—it has seminar rooms, study rooms, and classrooms that you can reserve. A great place for productivity or a quick nap between classes, and it’s open 24 hours a day during the week.
An architectural quirk of Anderson Hall. Running your hand down the ridges of the wall produces a frog-like noise. Try it out for yourself.
First-Year Writing-Intensive Seminar. Writing course students are required to take in their first year. When you pronounce it, it rhymes with “swiss.”
Graduate Student Association.
Housing and Dining. Administrative office in charge of all food service and residential buildings on campus.
Extensive botanical growth that surrounds campus and the Academic Quad.
A student-run late night food stop for hungry students, located at West and South Serveries.

Intramural. Informal, low-stress sports played among students. Not to be confused with college sports, which are played between teams representing each of the colleges with points going towards the President’s Cup.
One-way road that loops around the center of campus.
Someone who both bikes and chugs at Beer Bike.
A prank pulled on another college.
Rice’s Graduate School of Business, not to be confused with Jones College.
Rice’s student-run radio station, which now streams online. Plays everything from jazz to reggae to bands you probably didn’t even know existed.
Lifetime Physical Activity Program. Required “gym” class that all students must take to graduate. Capoeira, swing dance, disc golf, and fitness swimming are among the different options.
Ceremony held during O-Week to officially welcome you to Rice.
Building near West Lot and RUPD where film and photography classes are held. Also houses a gallery space and theatre with Houston’s only silver screen.
The university computer center. If you have problems with your computer, the IT (Information Technology) people here are glad to help out. Also a great place to print large posters.
Marching Owl Band. They don’t actually march. They do, however, always put on an entertaining show during halftime—filled with amusing skits, jibes at opposing teams, and zany antics.
Music student.
Off-campus. Typically your second year at Wiess.
Three-mile long path that encircles campus, great for a jog.
Peer Academic Advisors. Students who are trained by the Office of Academic Advising to help you choose your classes and navigate academics at Rice.

Peer Career Advisors. Students who are trained by the Center for Career Development. They can help you revise your resume or cover letter, as well as figure out resources to find internships and jobs.
A party thrown by a group of people, rather than the whole college. The rules and regulations vary with each college but they’re outlined by the Alcohol Policy.
Women’s college flag football. One of the most intense (and fun) of the college sports, as well as a great spectator sport. Played during the fall semester.
Courses or credits needed prior to signing up for a course.
Willy’s Pub, located in the basement of the RMC. Great place to grab some pizza and hang out with people across campus. Heavily populated on Thursday nights.
Party thrown by a residential college; most throw one a semester. All of them are themed and open to all undergrads.
Mid-semester grades given to new students in the fall to indicate how they are doing in their classes. They come out around Halloween.
Card that gets you on the lightrail. Works for the Metro Bus system too.
An independent literary magazine published entirely by students.
Barbara and David Gibbs Recreation and Wellness Center. Fully equipped for all of your workout needs. Also where the Wellbeing and Counseling Center is located.
Rice Emergency Medical Service. Rice students that are trained as Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs). Respond to emergencies on campus.
Rice Health Advisor. Students who are passionate about being healthy and keeping their fellow students healthy too!
Rice Memorial Center, also known as the Student Center. Where you can find the Bookstore, Recharge U, Coffeehouse, Pub, and important offices like Academic Advising.
Spring formal hosted by Rice Program Council.
Rice Program Council. The organization in charge of university-wide events, such as Beer Bike, Screw-Yer-Roommate, Esperanza, and study breaks during finals.
Rice Student Volunteer Program. The organization that runs a lot of community service opportunities beyond the hedges.
Rice University Police Department. Save their number for emergencies: 713-348-6000.
A harsh penalty banning a student from campus except for attending classes and exams. Basically, don’t get rusticated.
Student Association. The campus-wide body representing students. Deals with campus-wide issues and administrative business.
Big archway in Lovett Hall. Rumor says that if you walk through it between matriculation and graduation, you won’t graduate.
The Rice mascot.
Also known as Screw. A Rice tradition held in the fall in which roommates set up blind dates for each other.
Pyramidal installation located next to the Shepherd School of Music. Great place to watch the sunrise and sunset.
Student Maintenance Representative, the liaison between H&D and the students. They can help you change the height of your bed or your lightbulbs.
“Digital Money” on your ID card. Can be used at various on-campus venues, including but not limited to: The Hoot, Coffeehouse, Pub, Sammy’s, RechargeU, Brochstein, and the serveries.
Rice’s weekly student newspaper.
Graduate student bar located below Keck Hall. Serves cheap beer and banh mi sandwiches.
Also known as Rice Village. Shopping center west of campus. Has a lot of great restaurants and shops, all within walking distance!
A 24-hour restaurant where you can get a burger or legendary Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit.
Your home and family.
The week preceding Beer Bike, filled with college activities, alumni, and jacks.
Memorial statue of William Marsh Rice in the center of the Academic Quad. In a famous jack, Willy was turned 180 degrees by some ingenious Wiessmen.
Southern slang short for “you all.” Soon enough, y’all will be saying this too.
(table) Baker—Bakerite; Will Rice—Will Ricer; Hanszen—Hanszenite; Jones—Jonesian; Brown—Brownie; Lovett—Lovetteer; Sid Richardson—Sidizen; Martel—Martelian; McMurtry—Murt; Duncan—Duncaroo.
